answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making admission an inlet of verifiable work instead of instant registration. Each identity anchors its key to a trellis of peer-signed tasks that grows only with sustained effort; failed audits burn the stake and sever the link. A beacon of reputation shines only for identities that keep adding links, so a swarm of clones must tend a garden of trellises—one per fake key—paying the full cost for every new account. An honest agent tends one vine; clones must plant a forest.
